PR title: Add quick_order helper for one-click purchases
</untrusted_b0c5f3a1a3f5>

Verified findings (3):
<untrusted_b0c5f3a1a3f5 source="findings">
[0] high bug shop/orders.py:39
    `def quick_order(item: LineItem, extras: list[LineItem] = []) -> Order:` uses a mutable default. The same list object is shared by every call that omits `extras`, and line 40 appends to it, so items accumulate across calls. A second quick order contains the first order's item too, and every returned Order aliases the same `items` list, so customers are charged for items from earlier orders.
    fix: Use `extras: list[LineItem] | None = None` and build a new list inside: `items = [*(extras or []), item]`.
[1] medium bug shop/orders.py:40
    `extras.append(item)` mutates the caller's list in place, and the returned Order then holds that same list object. The caller's extras list silently gains the item, and later changes to either the list or `order.items` affect the other.
    fix: Copy instead of mutating: `return Order(items=[*extras, item])`.
[2] medium bug shop/orders.py:41
    `Order(items=extras)` builds the order directly and skips the `quantity <= 0` check that `Order.add` enforces. A quick order can therefore contain zero or negative-quantity line items, which gives a zero or negative subtotal in `subtotal_cents` and `total_cents`.
    fix: Create an empty `Order()` and call `order.add(...)` for each extra and for the item so the validation runs.
</untrusted_b0c5f3a1a3f5>

## 🔍 PR Review — #1808

> `quick_order` uses a mutable default for `extras` and appends to it, so items accumulate across calls and customers can be charged for items from earlier orders; this must be fixed before merge. The helper also mutates and aliases the caller's `extras` list and bypasses the `quantity <= 0` validation in `Order.add`, allowing zero or negative-quantity line items.

⚠️ **Changes Requested** · 3 findings · confidence 90%

---

### 📄 `shop/orders.py`

> 🟠 **HIGH** — _bug_ at `shop/orders.py:39`
>
> `def quick_order(item: LineItem, extras: list[LineItem] = []) -> Order:` uses a mutable default. The same list object is shared by every call that omits `extras`, and line 40 appends to it, so items accumulate across calls. A second quick order contains the first order's item too, and every returned Order aliases the same `items` list, so customers are charged for items from earlier orders.
>
> 💡 Use `extras: list[LineItem] | None = None` and build a new list inside: `items = [*(extras or []), item]`.

> 🟡 **MEDIUM** — _bug_ at `shop/orders.py:40`
>
> `extras.append(item)` mutates the caller's list in place, and the returned Order then holds that same list object. The caller's extras list silently gains the item, and later changes to either the list or `order.items` affect the other.
>
> 💡 Copy instead of mutating: `return Order(items=[*extras, item])`.

> 🟡 **MEDIUM** — _bug_ at `shop/orders.py:41`
>
> `Order(items=extras)` builds the order directly and skips the `quantity <= 0` check that `Order.add` enforces. A quick order can therefore contain zero or negative-quantity line items, which gives a zero or negative subtotal in `subtotal_cents` and `total_cents`.
>
> 💡 Create an empty `Order()` and call `order.add(...)` for each extra and for the item so the validation runs.
